newsitem.title: USA: Small group offers abortion pill across U.S..
newsitem.headline: Small group offers abortion pill across U.S..

text.p: A New York group announced on Wednesday it would expand its distribution of the French abortion pill to thousands of women nationwide while plans to market the drug in the United States were delayed.
Abortion Rights Mobilization (ARM), which already makes the drug available in several states, said it was opening a second outlet in New York and new sites in Florida and Texas.

ARM won approval from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) last year to use its version of the pill, popularly referred to as RU-486, in clinical trials. Women seeking non-surgical abortions receive the drug mifepristone free of charge as part of the trials but still pay doctors' fees.

The non-profit research group Population Council holds U.S. patent rights to the drug but its project has been stalled at least until 1998 because of a dispute with the manufacturer. The abortion pill is commercially available in France, Britain and Sweden.

"ARM pledges to continue making RU-486 and offering it to thousands more women nationwide so that no one will be denied access to this critical drug in the near future," the group's president, Lawrence Lader, said in a statement. As many as 10,000 women would be offered the drug, he said.

"These new clinics will bring RU-486 within reasonable traveling distance of all U.S. women," Lader said. He said 1,000 women in the United States have been successfully treated with RU-486 through ARM.
In the two-step process, women first take the abortion pill then a second drug days later to induce contractions.
Anti-abortion organizations in the United States have threatened to boycott any manufacturer of the drug. The maker of ARM's version of the abortion pill has been kept secret.

ARM medical director Eric Schaff of the University of Rochester Medical Center said the new sites would bring to 10 the number of clinics offering the pill nationwide. There are already clinics in Rochester, New York; New York City; San Francisco; Seattle; Kalispell, Montana; Bellevue, Nebraska, and Burlington, Vermont under the FDA-approved testing program.
